projects.name: Improving air quality in four large cities in North Macedonia by reducing emissions of pollutants, primarily PM2.5 and PM10
projects.description:
The EU for Clean Air Project (Project), funded by the European Union (EU) through the Instrument for Pre-accession Assistance (IPA), is designed to contribute to the improvement of air quality in North Macedonia and consequently decrease risks to human health.

The Project will achieve five results, the first one being related to improving heating systems through the replacement of obsolete and inefficient boilers in 70 air polluting public buildings at 43 locations in the cities of Skopje, Bitola, Kumanovo, and Tetovo, covering 200,000m2. The second result entails the procurement of six environmentally friendly buses that will reduce emissions of Carbon Monoxide (CO), Nitrogen Oxides (NOx) and particulate matter (PM) in the City of Skopje. Furthermore, six thousand tree seedlings will be procured as a part of the third result, in order to be planted in Skopje, Bitola, Tetovo and Kumanovo, contributing to reduction of Carbon Dioxide (CO2) in atmosphere, while also addressing particulate matter, and enhancing attractiveness of locations for leisure activities. The fourth Project result will deal with establishing the preconditions for extension of the heating network in Skopje through developing the Feasibility Study for the Further Expansion of the Skopje District Heating System (DHS) and the implementation of a public awareness raising campaign. Finally, within the fifth result, the Project will ensure procurement and the delivery and installation of three air quality monitoring stations.

projects.name: Enhanced land consolidation and mobility of the agricultural land market in North Macedonia
projects.description:
Under this sub-output, FAO, the European Union, and the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry, and Water Economy (MAFWE) have worked together to enhance the policy, legal, and institutional framework for agricultural land reforms. To address the issue of abandoned agricultural land, FAO supported MAFWE in 2022 and 2023 by analyzing existing tools and implementing best practices from Europe, including mediation for agricultural land leases.  FAO's report "Analysis of Land Abandonment and Development of Agricultural Land Markets in the Republic of North Macedonia - Conclusions and Policy Recommendations" identified key issues like poor land conditions, fragmented farms, inefficient irrigation, and youth outmigration, and offered recommendations for amendments to the Law on Agricultural Land and the Law on Privatization of State-Owned Land. This led to the inclusion of key measures in the April 2023 amendments to address land abandonment and strengthen agriculture.

Since 2017, the European Union and FAO have supported the Macedonian Ministry in addressing land fragmentation, small farm sizes, and inadequate agricultural infrastructure. Through the EU-FAO MAINLAND project (2017–2022), the National Land Consolidation Programme became operational, with initial land consolidation projects setting the stage for further advancements. Building on this foundation, the EU-FAO project "Enhancing Land Consolidation in North Macedonia" has continued to advance these efforts since 2022.
In Dabjani, construction works were finalized in 2024, including the rehabilitation and construction of access roads to the fields spanning 742 hectares of agricultural land. These improvements, funded by the European Union, enhanced connectivity and productivity for 85 landowners, facilitating more efficient agricultural practices and market access. Similarly, in Chiflik, FAO's efforts led to the adoption of a re-allotment plan by the majority of landowners, consolidating 156 fragmented hectares into more manageable and productive land parcels. This initiative directly benefited 395 farmers, laying the groundwork for sustainable agricultural development. Preparations are underway for EU-funded investments in Chiflik, including upgrades to access roads, irrigation systems, and drainage infrastructure, further strengthening rural resilience and productivity.  The end date of the project is 31 January 2026. Total expected funding for the full duration, including years beyond 2025 is USD 1,053,740.

projects.description:
This is the country’s fourth project under the GCF Readiness and Preparatory Support Programme titled "Strengthening Capacities and Developing Strategic Frameworks for a Low-Carbon and Climate-Resilient Society in North Macedonia"  Building upon the results of the first and second GCF readiness projects, FAO will further support the National Designated Authority for the Green Climate Fund and the GCF Strategic Advisory Committee to improve the country’s access to GCF funds by: 1) assisting a national entity in becoming a Direct Access Entity, 2) updating the GCF Country Work Programme, 3) strengthening capacity to monitor and report climate finance data, and 4) supporting the development of GCF-aligned projects for climate adaptation and mitigation. 

A key element of this project is FAO's support in preparing the prioritized GCF Concept Note for the five-year, Irrigation Development and Climate Adaptation initiative in two regions in North Macedonia. To support the development of the CN, in 2024, FAO initiated a pre-feasibility study for agricultural land consolidation and irrigation upgrades in Prilepsko Pole, covering 2,722 hectares and 3,335 landowners. The study will recommend the most suitable consolidation approach (voluntary or majority-based) and potential infrastructure investments. In addition, preparatory activities for building capacities of institutions involved in the national GCF coordination mechanism and other national stakeholders which are potential beneficiaries of GCF funds were ongoing during 2024. The project’s end date is 14 June 2026.  Total expected funding for the full duration, including years beyond 2025 is USD 497,000.

projects.description: The project aims to enhance the cybersecurity resilience of North Macedonia’s critical water infrastructure by implementing comprehensive cybersecurity measures. It focuses on building local capacity, setting benchmarks, and encouraging further investment into digital security across public utility companies and related sectors. The project will facilitate behavioral changes among target groups by raising awareness of cybersecurity risks and increasing technical capacity within water utilities. PUCs, municipalities, and government agencies will adopt stronger cybersecurity protocols, setting standards in line with EU legislation such as the NIS 2 Directive. This will lead to improved coordination, threat monitoring, and rapid response mechanisms. This shift in behavior will enhance overall system performance, safeguarding critical services from cyberattacks. The project will end in 2026 with total budget of 200.000 USD dedicated for the project.
projects.outcome: Output 4.2 Institutions capacitated for better planning, budgeting and service design and delivery

projects.name: National capacities for digital transformation of agriculture policy strengthened
projects.description: Under this project, FAO has supported the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Economy (MAFWE) in advancing the digital transformation of the agricultural sector. The overarching aim is to ensure that digitalization efforts effectively respond to the practical needs of farmers while strengthening evidence-based policymaking. In 2025, FAO completed a comprehensive situational analysis of digital transformation needs in agriculture in North Macedonia. This foundational assessment maps the current agricultural digital ecosystem, examining institutional capacities, existing tools, data systems, and broader sectoral readiness. The findings will serve as a critical basis for developing the country’s first National Strategy on the Digitalization of Agriculture and will guide FAO’s continued technical assistance to enhance key MAFWE digital solutions. These improvements will focus on strengthening data quality, quantity, interoperability, and overall functionality, in line with EU approximation requirements. Additionally, in 2025 FAO supported MAFWE in designing a specialized digital software solution for calculating the Cost of Production (CoP) for key agricultural products. The CoP is a vital indicator for assessing farm competitiveness, farmer incomes, the sustainability of production systems, and the country’s overall food production potential. The new tool will provide policymakers and farmers with a robust analytical instrument to evaluate and compare competitiveness across different agricultural systems and enterprises, contributing to more informed decision-making and improved sector performance.
projects.outcome: Output 1.5 Sustainable and competitive rural economy

projects.name: Empowering Adolescents Against Drugs under the Lions Quest “Skills for Adolescence” Prevention Programme in North Macedonia
projects.description:
UNODC: This initiative has trained 50 school specialists and 150 teachers from 50 primary schools across the country who will work with adolescents over the next two school years to implement the programme. The programme aims to strengthen the social and emotional skills of students aged 10 to 14. The training sessions were held from 27 October to 14 November 2025, in both Macedonian and Albanian languages, in the cities of Skopje, Strumica, Štip, Prilep, Kočani, and Gostivar. The implementation of the programme will include the training of teachers and school specialists who will deliver the programme, the evaluation of the programme through pre- and post-testing of students and process evaluation among the teachers, as well as the translation and cultural adaptation of the materials into Macedonian and Albanian languages.
More than a training, the “Skills for Adolescence” programme is a strategic investment in the wellbeing and resilience of young people. It empowers them to make healthy choices while building essential life skills (communication, critical thinking, conflict resolution and others) to prevent tobacco, alcohol, and drug use through evidence-based approach. It equips students with tools to resist peer pressure, make responsible decisions, and build positive and supportive relationships.

projects.name: Support for development of Biodiversity Finance Plan
projects.description:
The aim of the project is to support the country to enhance its financial management of biodiversity and ecosystems. UNESCO will contribute to this activity.
North Macedonia, located in Southeastern Europe, shares the regional vulnerability to climate change impacts such as rising temperatures, declining precipitation, and increasingly frequent extreme weather events. These challenges significantly affect ecosystems, agriculture, and communities, especially in rural areas where livelihoods are closely tied to natural resources. The country’s rich biodiversity, which includes critical habitats and species unique to the Balkan Peninsula, makes conservation efforts vital not only for North Macedonia but for global ecological health.

The country hosts several areas of ecological significance, some of which could qualify as UNESCO Biosphere Reserves or Geoparks, though limited resources and funding hinder their full potential. Protecting these sites is essential for sustainable development and aligning with regional and international conservation priorities.

However, like many countries in the region, North Macedonia faces significant barriers to accessing international climate finance mechanisms such as the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the Global Environment Facility (GEF). Complex application processes, limited technical capacity, and challenges in coordinating stakeholders often prevent the effective mobilization of necessary funds. Additionally, existing financial mechanisms for biodiversity conservation, particularly in areas of international ecological importance, are underutilized. This creates challenges for the management and protection of these areas.

To address these gaps, capacity-building efforts for stakeholders managing ecologically significant sites are critical. Ensuring they are equipped to access and manage climate and biodiversity financing can enhance the country's ability to achieve climate resilience and conservation goals. Such actions align with North Macedonia’s commitments under global frameworks like the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 13 (Climate Action) and SDG 15 (Life on Land), as well as UNESCO’s Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme and the International Geoscience and Geoparks Programme (IGGP). By tackling funding and technical capacity challenges, North Macedonia can position itself as a leader in integrating climate action and biodiversity conservation into sustainable development strategies, ensuring both ecological and community resilience
projects.outcome: Output 3.2 Integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources

projects.description: Developing a roadmap for upgrading the national animal identification, registration and traceability system (Phase 1 - finalized in 2022 - FAO project TCP/MCD/3804/C3). Based on the developed technical documentation and implementation roadmap (Phase I) starting from 2023 (project TCP/MCD/3902) FAO has been supporting the FVA to put the new National Animal Information System in use (Phase 2) unlocking several modules and features presently not available in the obsolete Veterinary Information System (FAO project TCP/MCD 3902 - with end date 31.12.2025). Under this project, FAO is providing technical assistance to the Food and Veterinary Agency (FVA) to harmonize North Macedonia’s National Animal Health and Food Safety System (NAITS) with EU standards. This upgraded system will enable efficient recording, analysis, and utilization of critical animal data throughout their lifecycle, enhancing management and traceability in the livestock sector. projects.name: Improved maternal and newborn health outcomes through enhanced implementation of effective perinatal care in maternities, systematic reporting and analysis of maternal mortalities and morbidities and implementation of evidenced- based and standardized policies
projects.description:
In 2021: Support for implementation of the perinatal care pilots in Bitola and Tetovo regions, including capacity building, management of data and information, establishment of regulatory framework and system for monitoring and evaluation; Implementation of perinatal mortality audit for 2020 to be able to generate evidence for highlighting areas that need to be addressed in order to improve the care for mothers and their infants during pregnancy, childbirth and the neonatal period.
In 2022: 
• Support in the operationalization of the Obstetric Surveillance and Response System (OSRS), for anonymous review of nearly-missed maternal lives
• Finalization of the trainings for Effective Perinatal Care in the pilot networks and  continuation of the support for implementation of the perinatal networks of care in other 4 regions in the country based on the pilot experience in Bitola and Tetovo region, through technical guidance and capacity building activities as well as activities for management of data and information, establishment of regulatory framework and system for monitoring and evaluation;                                                          
•Support for digitalization of the data collection for the perinatal death 
•Support in implementation of the perinatal death review (audit)    
•Support to Perinatal care masterplan 2030 - development of standards and capacity development for professionals for perinatal transport, training for neonatologists
•Development of SRHR Action Plan for 2022-2023
•Review & update of the Action Plan for Response of the Health System in times of crises (MISP)
•Operationalization of the Virtual Contraception Platform (VIC))
In 2023:
Continue the technical support for implementation of the perinatal death surveys and for implementation of the Master Plan for Perinatal Care; Initiation of activities for digitalization of collection of the data for perinatal death reviews; Technical support in the introduction of anonymous review of critical cases (near-miss maternal deaths – OSRS). Continue capacity building through EPC training for personnel of the EPC pilot facilities.

In 2024: (WHO/UNFPA/UNICEF) Support the implementation of the National Master Plan for Perinatal Care and completion of the perinatal mortality audits for 2021 and 2022; Support the Ministry of Health to develop the National Strategy on Sexual and Reproductive Health 2030;

framework.name: Sustained and inclusive economic and social development

children.name: Outcome 1: Inclusive Prosperity
children.description:
Outcome 1: The UN entities contribution to inclusive prosperity of North Macedonia focus on creating new productive, full-time jobs that are resilient to any sustained or future shocks, supporting the authorities to make growth more robust, sustainable and inclusive. Interventions will prioritize LNOB groups of people who will be equipped with skills and capacities to enjoy and have equal access to full, productive and freely chosen employment, thus reducing inequalities, including income inequality. 

The UN entities contribution to inclusive prosperity of North Macedonia focus on creating new productive, full-time jobs that are resilient to any sustained or future shocks, supporting the authorities to make growth more robust, sustainable and inclusive. Interventions will prioritize LNOB groups of people who will be equipped with skills and capacities to enjoy and have equal access to full, productive and freely chosen employment, thus reducing inequalities, including income inequality.

children.name: Output 1.1: Sustainable enterprises created as generators of employment
children.description: Output 1.1: Sustainable enterprises created as generators of employment, through strengthened value chains and increased capacities to adopt new business models. Throughout 2021, under this output, UN will work with the stakeholders on creation of productive and competitive enterprises as generators of employment, decent work and innovations, by delivering tailored interventions for start-ups, formalization of economy and strengthening value chains. Focusing on youth at policy and at operational level, UN will also work with Government to enhance SMEs development and innovation ecosystem, including by introducing know-how and building capacity for technical modernization, while supporting public-private partnership to address the challenges of the adjusting employment patterns.

children.name: Output 1.2 Jobs for women and vulnerable people
children.description: Outcome 1.2: Women and vulnerable/excluded persons benefit from supportive environment through tailored employment measures and a more dynamic and inclusive skilling system that responds to labour market needs for all people. Under this output, in 2021, UN will assist the Government to develop supportive environment for women and vulnerable/excluded persons through tailored activation and employment support measures and a more dynamic and inclusive skilling system that responds to labour market needs of all people. In that context, UN will pursue advocacy interventions to eliminate legal and administrative barriers to the access and inclusion of asylum seekers in job market, including evaluation of skills & diplomas.  Furthermore, UN will develop, support and promote life-long learning models among socially excluded groups, including people with disabilities, prisons inmates and Roma people with special focus on women.

children.name: Output 1.3 Enhanced policies and regulatory environment
children.description: Output 1.3: Enhanced and gender-responsive policy and regulatory measures that foster entrepreneurship and financing for inclusive and green growth. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will work to enhance and harmonize policy and regulatory measures with the International labour standards and EU acquis, in order to foster gender-responsive, entrepreneurial and green growth. To achieve this, UN will support social dialogue as an essential element of the European social model, assisting the government and social partners to bridge the legal and implementation gaps in compliance with International Labour Standards and the EU acquis. The UN will facilitate tripartite consultations and give technical support for drafting the new National Employment Strategy and the new Action Plan on Youth Employment. Furthermore, UN will promote alternative social services and policy reforms for vulnerable, and enhance ESA’s capacity to provide services with strengthened consultation and environment that promotes future jobs and skills requested by the market. UN will work on developing and maintaining of MIS for more competitive, inclusive, efficient and resilient agri-food systems, as well as on optimizing the opportunities from Diaspora engagement.

children.name: Output 1.4 Under-employment, informality and protection at work
children.description: Output 1.4: Improved quality of employment through measures for transition to formality and adequate protection at work in compliance with international labour standards. Limited activities under this output will be carried out during 2021, focusing on improving the quality of employment with pilot measures to reduce informality, technical support for drafting the new labour legislation,  and promotion of the ratification of the new international labour standards.

children.name: Output 1.5 Sustainable and competitive rural economy
children.description: Output 1.5: Policies and capacities strengthened for sustainable and competitive rural economy aligned with EU, with focus on small farms and women farmers. Under this output, during 2021, UN will continue its work on strengthening evidence-based policies and institutional capacities for sustainable and competitive rural economy aligned with EU, focusing on land consolidation and implementation of other land market instruments, supporting small farm-holders and women farmers with integrated local development initiatives piloted in selected municipalities, sustainable production technologies, income diversification, and improving smallholders’ access to markets,  value chains and enhanced rural services.

children.name: Outcome 2: Quality Services for All
children.description:
Outcome 2: By 2025, people in North Macedonia have universal access to rights-based quality social services – healthcare, education, and necessary social and child protection - rooted in systems resilient to emergencies.

UN entities have committed to support the country’s social development through activities that will strive to achieve universal access to rights-based quality social services – healthcare, education, and  social and child protection, including in emergencies. While the activities will be targeting all people in the country, the nature of this outcome entails focus on the most vulnerable ones, those that are usually left behind.

children.name: Output 2.1 Universal access to affordable high quality health services
children.description: Output 2.1: Health system is strengthened to provide universal access to affordable high quality and people-centred services to promote healthy lifestyles and address population-specific health needs and risk factors, including in emergencies. The work of all involved UN entities in 2021 will aim to continue supporting the health care system for efficient delivery of affordable high quality and people-centered essential health services, including support in responding to the COVID-19 pandemic, in line with the Covid-19 Response Framework, developed in 2020.   UN will work on improvement of the health care coverage, through pilot interventions in primary health care. It will focus on all levels of productive health services, such as family planning, maternal health and cervical cancer prevention. These efforts will be coupled with improving prevention of specific conditions, awareness raising and improved access to services for women and girls and other vulnerable categories such are refugees, migrants and stateless people. In addition, functional analysis of home visiting system and pediatric care will be undertaken, Vaccine hesitancy at national level will be tackled, etc.  Extensive activities for capacity building of health workforce will be carried out in parallel. UN entities will further work on strengthening of the perinatal health care system through Implementation of various actions from the National Master Plan for perinatal care and provide policy support by strengthening the evidence-based policy making processes on health inequity, institutionalization of the National Health Accounts, Health financing and financial risk protection; development of parenting strategy; reversing childhood obesity trend and others. Finally, in the area of health, UN entities will support accelerated digitalization of the health system by introducing digital mental health tools; digitalization of the reporting and recording system for home visiting nurses and the vaccination registry system.

children.name: Output 2.2 Quality and affordable education
children.description: Output 2.2: Quality and affordable education is provided in trauma-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive learning environments to children and young people in the country to raise learning outcomes, enable their socio-emotional development and empower them with skills for transition to the labour market. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will provide support to the education reforms aimed at providing quality and affordable education in trauma-informed, gender-responsive and inclusive learning environments to children and young people in the country to raise learning outcomes, enable their socio-emotional development and empower them with skills for transition to the labour market. UN entities will focus on teachers capacity development, creation of digital and inclusive learning tools and resources that are in line with the pre-primary, primary and secondary education curricula, Improvements of WASH capacities in schools, awareness raising to remove barriers to inclusion of children with disabilities, as well as on piloting of the comprehensive sexuality education in selected schools. The entities will also undertake preparatory activities for introduction of youth initiative in municipalities that measures youth engagement and develop advocacy, knowledge exchange and community engagement on issues of interest and benefit of youth. Refugees, asylum seekers and stateless children will be supported to access the appropriate level of education.

children.name: Output 2.3 Social protection of all persons in need
children.description: Output 2.3: Social protection system is resilient to external shocks and strengthened to deliver progressively improved services to all persons in need, especially to those left behind. in 2021, under this output, Activities aimed to enhance the social protection system to increase its resilience to external shocks and to progressively strengthen the delivery of improved services to all persons in need, especially to those left behind will also be part of the UN agenda for 2021. The activities will include: enhanced provision of social protection services to vulnerable categories of migrants, asylum seekers, refugees and stateless persons; new parenting programmes and helpline services including parenting services campaigns; support of the child-care system through capacity development of foster and kindship care, and creating community-based support system; development of community-based care/services for children and families experiencing adversity; Continuous child protection and GBV services and psychosocial support to children and families in emergencies as well as establishment of regional centers for ICF-based assessment for additional educational, health and social support to children and youth. Evaluation on UNICEF interventions for inclusion of children with disabilities will be undertaken, as well as analysis of multi-dimensional poverty aimed to provide better evidence for policy improvements, including enhancement of the national statistical system. Support to the introduction of social work case management mentoring and supervision will be provided, as well as technical assistance in the development of integrated MIS on social cash transfers and social services.

children.name: Output 2.4 Eliminate all forms of violence
children.description: Output 2.4: Improved multi-sectoral response to prevent and address all forms of violence based on victims/survivor-centred approach, including harmful practices and discriminatory gender norms and stereotypes. in 2021, under this output, UN entities will provide dedicated support for improved multisectoral response to prevent and address all forms of violence, using victims/survivor-centered approach and through operationalization of the Law on Prevention and Protection of Violence Against Women and Domestic Violence. UN entities will support the relevant partners in collection of disaggregated data and evidence for defining requirements and specifications of a system for GBV data integration. Service providers will be capacitated to provide better multi-sectorial response to GBV by implementing the standards enshrined in CEDAW and the Istanbul Convention, while the Civil Society Organizations will be capacitated to support the development and implementation of laws and policies in line with CEDAW and the Istanbul Convention and to promote favorable social norms, attitudes and behaviors to prevent violence against women and girls. UN entities will also work with community figures/leaders mobilized to enhance gender equality and women empowerment and design and implement cross-sectoral communication for development initiatives to address barriers to optimal thriving and flourishing of children.

framework.name: Climate action, natural resources and disaster risk management

children.name: Outcome 3: Healthy Environment
children.description:
Outcome 3: By 2025, people in North Macedonia benefit from ambitious climate action, sustainably managed natural resources and well-preserved biodiversity through good environmental governance and disaster resilient communities.

Over the period 2021-2025, the UN entities contribution to healthy environment will focus on policy support, capacity building and community actions for low-emission development and multi-sector resilience to climate change; sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources; prevention and response to air pollution threats, effective disaster risk reduction and response; waste reduction and efficient waste management, and reducing impact of the unsustainable farming practices on the lake/river watersheds.

children.name: Output 3.1 Low-emissions development and climate change resilience
children.description: Output 3.1: The enabling policy, regulatory environment, capacities at central and local level and community actions strengthened for low-emission development and multi-sector resilience to climate change. In 2021, the UN intends to support to country on policy development and implementation (support for development of new strategic policy documents  such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and greater implementation/enforcement of environment and climate change legislation, EU Chapter 27 requirements) and National Adaptation Plan, and implementation of priority measures), climate finance and green economy (support to Green Climate Fund (GCF) national mechanism and programme, potential implementation of the Green Financing Facility, a new vehicle to provide financing to end consumers for renewable energy and energy efficiency investments, assessment of potential for expansion of the use of clean technologies and creation of green jobs, acceleration of market transformation for industrial energy efficiency), and climate-smart agriculture (new technologies piloted, tools for evidence-based policy) and on public awareness and knowledge increasing. In addition, UN will support the introduction of environment/green education within the ongoing primary education reform, including by development of appropriate content, building capacities of more than 150 teachers, more than 50 education inspectors and raising awareness on env. and climate change of of the general public (>100,000 people).

children.name: Output 3.2 Integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources
children.description: Output 3.2: Solutions are identified and scaled-up at central and local levels for integrated, sustainable and inclusive management of natural resources (water, land, forests, biodiversity). in 2021, under this output, UN will provide support with a diverse set of activities related to land, forest and biodiversity protection (2 new protected areas mgt plans, increased forest area, policy for sustainable land tenure and management, 3’000 ha with sustainable land management practices, various activities for protection of forest vegetation, reptiles and amphibians, and sustainable use of non-timber forest products), enhanced food safety and quality standards in dairy sector, activities for greener Skopje (biotope mapping, green cadastre update, construction of green roofs, development of water strategy etc.), increased proportion of transboundary basin with operational arrangement for water cooperation, and cultural and natural heritage protection (increased total expenditure per capita (public and private), various activities to protect Cultural and Natural Heritage of the Ohrid Region. Last but not least, activities that ensure lake/river watersheds protection through promoting sustainable farming practices (Prespa: + 200 ha, +150 households, Strumica River Basin), sustainable tourism offer (+40 B&Bs in Prespa) and active transboundary governance of Prespa Lake Watershed (active Management Body and Water Management Working Group) will be continued.

children.name: Output 3.3 Air pollution in urban areas decreased
children.description:
Output 3.3: Capacities at central and local levels are strengthened to prevent and respond to the air pollution threats and health consequences in most vulnerable communities. 

In 2021 the UN’s support will focus on providing evidence for policy (preparation of Source Apportionment Study, Analyzing interlinkages between human mobility and air pollution study), raising public awareness (public awareness on air pollution causes and effects), improvement of the monitoring system for air pollution in Skopje, and demonstration/proof of concept for measures to reduce the air pollution in the City of Skopje (implementation of  energy efficiency measures in households in Lisiche settlement), support to regulatory changes to support policies for reduction of air pollution.

children.name: Output 3.4 Effective disaster risk reduction and response
children.description: Output 3.4: Capacities at central and local levels are strengthened to identify multi-hazard risks and to plan, finance and implement effective disaster risk reduction and response, including human displacement, in line with the Sendai framework. A comprehensive portfolio of DRR activities is planned for 2021, with focus on field activities (specific activities on increased resilience of Agri sector, improved flood risk management of the Drini River Basin (transboundary) and in the Polog region), capacity building of civil servants (capacity building on DRR (10 civil servants, urban focus) and on human displacement caused by disasters (200 civil servants, central level focus)), DRR finance (Flood Risk Financing and Flood Risk Transfer, Increase of public expenditures in DRR), early warning system (early warning system established in Polog region, 2 data informed and gender responsive DRR plans).

children.name: Output 3.5 Waste reduction and efficient waste management
children.description: Output 3.5: National and local capacities strengthened, and awareness increased for waste reduction and efficient waste management (chemical, water, municipal waste, hazardous waste, medical waste – including in rural areas). In 2021, the UN will continue to providing sizable support in the cleanup of environmental hotspots (Ohis Factory Complex: HCH waste, small waste basin).

children.name: Outcome 4: Good Governance
children.description:
Outcome 4: By 2025, people in North Macedonia benefit from improved rule of law; evidence-based, anticipatory and gender-responsive policies; greater social cohesion; and effective service delivery by transparent, accountable and responsive institutions.

The UN in North Macedonia works with the government and whole of society towards effective, accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels, and promotion and protection of human rights for all, focusing on groups that have been left behind, or are at risk of being left behind, including women, children, youth not in education, employment or training (NEET), persons with disabilities, Roma and other ethnic communities, refugees, asylum seekers, migrants, internally displaced persons (IDPs) and stateless, LGBTI persons, people in rural areas and small farmers, older persons and other vulnerable groups.

children.name: Output 4.1 Rule of Law, Access to Justice and Human rights
children.description: Output 4.1: The rule of law, access to justice, and protection and promotion of human rights for all, especially those left behind advanced through inclusive and gender-responsive legal, policy, and institutional frameworks and strengthened capacities. Throughout 2021, the UN will strengthen its partnership and capacity of state and non-state actors to accelerate policy and institutional reforms advancing the rule of law, gender equality, and access to justice and services responsive to those in need. The empowerment of people left behind to claim and seek the protection of their rights and effective free legal aid will be central to these efforts.

children.name: Output 4.2 Institutions capacitated for better planning, budgeting and service design and delivery
children.description:
Output 4.2: Capacities of central and local governments strengthened to:
a)	better plan, budget, monitor and track expenditure and leverage resources in a gender-responsive manner in support of accelerated sustainable development 
b)	improve design and efficient delivery of quality public services (targeting excluded groups, including refugee /migration management)
with improved social accountability and participation in decision-making.  

UN will contribute in developing and implementing national strategies and legislation in line with international and EU standards in areas of non-discrimination, gender equality, migration management, judicial reform, anti-corruption, arms control and fight against organized crime. The government technical skills to engage in the EU accession negotiations will be stepped up, along with the support to the EU acquis approximation process.
  
At central and local government level, the UN will accelerate efficient delivery of quality public services targeting excluded groups and their social and economic vulnerabilities, thus improving the overall trust and accountability of institutions. Promoting transparency and participation in the decision-making will result in better planning, budgeting and monitoring, while leveraging resources in a gender-responsive and child-sensitive manner. The UN will support primary school optimization and improving the budgetary allocations system in primary and secondary education, as well as youth consultations and adolescent participation and empowerment.

children.name: Output 4.3 Improved participatory policy making based on better data
children.description: Output 4.3: Increased utilization of foresight and quality and disaggregated data for improved forward looking, evidence-based, results-oriented and transparent policy-making, responsive to the rights of women, men, girls and boys and vulnerabilities of the groups left behind, at all levels and in all contexts, including humanitarian. In 2021, UN will support national stakeholders to promote evidence-based policy making and long‐term strategic visioning that will accelerate SDGs mainstreaming and shaping of a National Development Strategy. To this end, foresight methods for strategic multi-year planning, responsive to the rights of women, men, girls and boys, and vulnerabilities of the groups left behind or at risk of being left behind in all contexts, including humanitarian, will be promoted. Data collection and analysis mechanisms will be strengthened as a key precondition for evidenced-based and result-oriented policy making.

children.name: Output 4.4 Improved social cohesion and trust building
children.description: Output 4.4: Social cohesion and trust improved through dialogue and meaningful participation by youth, women, ethnic and religious minorities, refugees, and other vulnerable groups. UN interventions are designed to support societal transformation for more active and responsible individual and community approaches to sustainable and inclusive development. The UN support to good governance, human rights and gender equality will ultimately contribute to strengthening the social cohesion and trust, through improved dialogue and meaningful participation.

children.name: Output 4.5 Asset recovery and countering corruption
children.description: Output 4.5: Enhanced national and local capacities in asset recovery and countering corruption in public life through better enforcement of anti-corruption laws and preventive measures.
